title: Salford girl, 7, wins national Lowry art prize

evidence_packet.title: Salford girl, 7, wins national Lowry art prize
evidence_packet.lead: Mia says she is "really happy" to have her artwork on display in the Lowry museum
evidence_packet.summary: Mia says she is "really happy" to have her artwork on display in the Lowry museum
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A seven-year-old girl has won a national competition for her artwork which was inspired by LS Lowry Mia, of Salford, was picked as the winner from 600 entries to the 2026 Copley Prize, an annual art competition run by the Lowry theatre and gallery Her artwork, titled A Man Going To Work, is now hanging in the Andrew Law Galleries, alongside the famous paintings by Lowry himself, and will remain on display for the next 12 months Mia said: "I feel so happy that my work will be in a real art gallery." Every year primary school-aged children from across the UK are invited to submit artwork inspired by LS Lowry to Lowry's Copley Prize Mia's work was chosen as this year's overall winner by Alison and Noel Copley who are huge admirers of LS Lowry's work and long-standing supporters of the Lowry's programmes for children and young people

title: Wasp spider spotted in North West for first time, Chester Zoo says

evidence_packet.title: Wasp spider spotted in North West for first time, Chester Zoo says
evidence_packet.lead: Wasp spiders pose no threat to humans, despite their warning colours and size, Chester Zoo says
evidence_packet.summary: Wasp spiders pose no threat to humans, despite their warning colours and size, Chester Zoo says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A brightly coloured wasp spider has reached the north-west of England for the first time, conservationists have said The large black and yellow spider was recorded during a survey on Chester Zoo's estate, with a zoo spokesperson saying this was "the first time this fascinating mimic has reached the area" Wasp spiders have only previously been spotted in the south of England but zoo bosses believe this arrival, who they have nicknamed Wendy, is a sign that climate change was impacting UK wildlife A zoo spokesperson said: "Despite their warning colours and size, wasp spiders pose no threat to humans." Zoo conservationists said the wasp spider's discovery highlighted the need to make space for nature The discovery was made by Chester Zoo conservationists working with RECORD, Cheshire's local environmental records centre, and was subsequently confirmed by an expert from the British Arachnological Society, the zoo said

Kenneth Harrison co-founded Medicina Ltd, a legitimate company selling medical goods, in 1991 but over the years began to regard proper testing and certification as merely "red tape" and an inconvenience, a court heard. Manchester Crown Court was told he had also encouraged his staff to cover up his dishonesty by selling goods with false safety approval markings. The 70-year-old, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, was convicted of five fraud offences between 2010 and 2014, following a 10-week trial earlier this year. The hearing was told Harrison had sold goods bearing false "CE" markings to hospitals and clinics in the UK and worldwide, misleading buyers into believing they had passed EU-wide safety and regulatory approval. Judge Timothy Smith sentenced Harrison to 175 hours of unpaid work alongside the suspended jail sentence. 'Deliberate and dishonest' He also disqualified the him from being a company director for eight years. The judge told him: "The fact that you acted deliberately and dishonestly to cover fraudulent conduct is a matter of significant aggravation. "You were prepared to invite staff, including your own son, to lie and hide your own conduct and regulatory failings. "You have lost your good name and reputation." Harrison's firm sold feeding pumps which were used in neonatal intensive care units and special care baby units to feed very sick newborn babies directly into their stomachs. title: Early release scheme won't work without us, says ex-prisoner

evidence_packet.title: Early release scheme won't work without us, says ex-prisoner
evidence_packet.lead: Jamie Dale spent more than 11 years in prison and now runs a support network for former inmates
evidence_packet.summary: Jamie Dale spent more than 11 years in prison and now runs a support network for former inmates
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A former prisoner who runs a support network for ex-offenders said government plans to release inmates early would fail to ease prison overcrowding without support from people who had experienced the system themselves Jamie Dale, 47, from Rochdale, in Greater Manchester, spent more than 11 years in prison for his involvement in organised crime. He now runs the Old Lags Network, which aims to cut reoffending and bridge the gap between prison and the community He said many prisoners "fall through the cracks" after release "Most of the people who return quite quickly have not got great family networks," he said Dale said involving ex-offenders in developing solutions would "drastically reduce the amount of people being recalled to prison" "A lot of them can just end up sleeping on the streets," he said

title: Bakery owner calls for Budget help for firms

evidence_packet.title: Bakery owner calls for Budget help for firms
evidence_packet.lead: Frankie Dyer has written to the prime minister urging Budget support for businesses
evidence_packet.summary: Frankie Dyer has written to the prime minister urging Budget support for businesses
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The owner of a bakery in Manchester has urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to give the hospitality industry a 'fighting chance' as it struggles to keep up with increasing prices Barbakan Deli is an artisan bakery and deli in Chorlton that has been at the heart of the community for the last 62 years. However, it is struggling to keep up with its bills, despite turning over more than £2.3m a year In an open letter to the prime minister, owner Frankie Dyer said there is "nowhere left to squeeze" and asked for independent businesses to be considered in the upcoming Budget A Treasury spokesperson said decisions on tax are "a matter for the Chancellor to set out at fiscal events" In the letter, which has since been widely seen by nearly a million people online, Dyer wrote: "Since Covid, independent businesses like ours have dragged ourselves through crisis after crisis." "Energy prices. Fuel costs. Food shortages. Inflation. Increasing wages. Pension contributions. Corporation Tax at 25%. Business rates. And then the enormous additional cost of the increase in Employer National Insurance."

title: Middleton residents campaign to keep beloved kickpitch

evidence_packet.title: Middleton residents campaign to keep beloved kickpitch
evidence_packet.lead: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
evidence_packet.summary: Residents in the Langley Estate of Middleton are campaigning to keep their community kickpitch in the area
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Residents in Middleton are campaigning for a replacement football pitch after plans were announced to turn the existing site into a car park Campaigners say the pitch in Burnside Crescent on the Langley Estate is a community hub as well as somewhere people can play football and other sports The pitch, which is next to the Burnside Centre, is one of three on the estate, and the car park will be for the centre Families say they have been told replacement facilities will be provided at Rochdale AFC and Rochdale Council's planned Football and Community Wellbeing Hub at Bowlee Playing Fields. But they are campaigning for the new pitch to be created on land next to the original The Burnside Centre said it understands why people are disappointed to see the pitch decommissioned, but said one of the reasons the decision was made related to concerns about antisocial behaviour It added: "The pitch, which dates back to the late 1990s, had reached the end of its expected lifespan and required significant investment to remain operational."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A brightly coloured wasp spider has reached the north-west of England for the first time, conservationists have said The large black and yellow spider was recorded during a survey on Chester Zoo's estate, with a zoo spokesperson saying this was "the first time this fascinating mimic has reached the area" Wasp spiders have only previously been spotted in the south of England but zoo bosses believe this arrival, who they have nicknamed Wendy, is a sign that climate change was impacting UK wildlife A zoo spokesperson said: "Despite their warning colours and size, wasp spiders pose no threat to humans." evidence_packet.evidence_text: A company director who sold £500,000 of illegal medical devices has been given a three-year suspended jail sentence Kenneth Harrison co-founded Medicina Ltd, a legitimate company selling medical goods, in 1991 but over the years began to regard proper testing and certification as merely "red tape" and an inconvenience, a court heard Manchester Crown Court was told he had also encouraged his staff to cover up his dishonesty by selling goods with false safety approval markings The 70-year-old, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, was convicted of five fraud offences between 2010 and 2014, following a 10-week trial earlier this year The hearing was told Harrison had sold goods bearing false "CE" markings to hospitals and clinics in the UK and worldwide, misleading buyers into believing they had passed EU-wide safety and regulatory approval Judge Timothy Smith sentenced Harrison to 175 hours of unpaid work alongside the suspended jail sentence

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The owner of a bakery in Manchester has urged Prime Minister Andy Burnham to give the hospitality industry a 'fighting chance' as it struggles to keep up with increasing prices Barbakan Deli is an artisan bakery and deli in Chorlton that has been at the heart of the community for the last 62 years. However, it is struggling to keep up with its bills, despite turning over more than £2.3m a year In an open letter to the prime minister, owner Frankie Dyer said there is "nowhere left to squeeze" and asked for independent businesses to be considered in the upcoming Budget A Treasury spokesperson said decisions on tax are "a matter for the Chancellor to set out at fiscal events" In the letter, which has since been widely seen by nearly a million people online, Dyer wrote: "Since Covid, independent businesses like ours have dragged ourselves through crisis after crisis." evidence_packet.evidence_text: The route has been revised of a proposed gas pipeline that would see compressed carbon dioxide stored under the sea in a project dubbed dangerous and potentially devastating to the countryside Peak Cluster, a joint initiative between four cement firms, said the changes followed consultation and technical assessments Two arms would begin near Hope, Derbyshire and Cauldon, Staffordshire, joining together near Marton in Cheshire before heading to Hoylake on the Wirral The £5bn government-backed scheme features a buried pipeline as well as above-ground installations, but people living along its route are unhappy, and one councillor has described it as a "dangerous, dangerous thing" As well as altering its course in some areas, the proposals have reduced the width of the route earmarked of the pipeline from 300m (328 yards) to approximately 100m (109 yards) The new plans will be the subject of consultations in Staffordshire, Derbyshire and Cheshire in November, with the proposals for the Wirral due to be the focus in January

evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Manchester EasyJet flight makes sharp U-turn after declaring emergency over North Sea EasyJet said the flight returned to Manchester Airport due to "a technical issue with the aircraft" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inno An EasyJet flight heading to
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester EasyJet flight makes sharp U-turn after declaring emergency over North Sea EasyJet said the flight returned to Manchester Airport due to "a technical issue with the aircraft" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inno An EasyJet flight heading to Germany has made a sharp mid-air U-turn and returned to Manchester after declaring an emergency over the North Sea The flight, EZY32GY, from Manchester to Hamburg sparked concern on Wednesday evening (September 23) after declaring an emergency mid-air and turning back near Amsterdam According to Flight Radar, the aircraft took off at 7.15pm - one hour and 15 minutes after its scheduled departure time. The flight then squawked 7700 and turned around approximately 30 minutes after takeoff Squawk 7700 is the universal aviation transponder code used by pilots to signal a general in-flight emergency The real-time aviation alert service Squawk wrote on X shortly after 8pm: "An AIRBUS A-320 (EZY32GY) is squawking 7700 — declaring an emergency at 34,000 ft near Amsterdam, Netherlands."

Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 18:52, 23 Se A longstanding Oldham councillor and former Mayor has announced he will not stand for re-election when voters go to the polls again in 2027 Coun Dr Zahid Chauhan OBE was first elected as a Labour councillor for the council ward of Alexandra in 2013. He is an NHS GP and the founder of the Homeless Friendly charity During his time as councillor, he served as Mayor for two years, was awarded Honorary Freedom of the Borough of Oldham , and recently campaigned on parking issues at the Royal Oldham Hospital. He has also previously served as the cabinet member overseeing health and social care In this role, Coun Chauhan said he was proud of making national history by launch a pop-up vaccination clinic for people experiencing homelessness. He also made sure two nurses Jean Purdy and Muriel Harris who had helped bring the first test-tube baby into the world were recognis After announcing he will be stepping down in May 2027, Coun Chauhan’s time as councillor will now end at the next set of local elections

And he believes its down to weight loss medications such as Mounjaro Writing on X he said: "You can tell Ozempic and Mounjaro are popular... in our Timpson shops we have seen a 680% increase in the number of free holes in customers belts we've been doing this year." Some estimates suggest around 2.4 million people in the UK are prescribed weight loss medications . The vast majority of people taking the drugs semaglutide (Wegovy for weight loss or Ozempic for diabetes) and Mounjaro pay privately owing to restrictions on who can access the med In June, the medicines regulator approved Wegovy in tablet form

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport EasyJet offered dad £150 after 11-hour Manchester Airport delay, what came next was a 'kick in the face' 'I wouldn't fly with easyJet again' Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 05:57, 24 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Stephen Gilfoyl A dad who says his family lost out on a day of their £4,000 holiday after a diversion and delays of around 11 hours has hit out after he was initially offered just £150 compensation Stephen Gilfoyle, 39, was due to fly out from Manchester Airport to Antalya in Turkey with easyJet on August 31 for a week-long all-inclusive package holiday with his wife and eight-year-old daughter However, shortly before they were due to board a coach to take them to the plane for their 7:45am flight, they were told they would be delayed as the captain was 'ill.' After a delay of two hours, they did board the plane, but once they were seated, they were told they would be further delayed due to ' weather problems.' They eventually took off five hours late; however, Stephen said the disruption did not end there Just two hours into the four-hour flight, he says, they were told they would be diverting to Milan as members of the cabin crew would go over their allotted hours if they continued to their destination

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Council ‘Too big’ and an ‘absolute shambles', but 300 new homes have just been been approved Councillors agreed the site is an 'eyesore' and needs 'sorting out' but some did not think this was the right approach Comments News Hannah Richardso Councillors fear the project is ‘too big’ and parking plans are an ‘absolute shambles', but plans for 300 new homes have been approved for Old Trafford The plan flats on the site of a ‘derelict’ petrol station and disused multi-storey car park in Chester Road left Trafford council’s planning committee divided on Tuesday night (September 22). The scheme will see the existing structures demolished and two blocks of 286 apartments While all on the committee agreed that the ‘eyesore’ land needed to be redeveloped, not everyone was convinced that this scheme was the right solution. The debate saw a vote to reject the proposal defeated Concerns were raised by some members that the plan was ‘too big’ for the area and would ‘dwarf everything else’. The provision of just seven parking spaces to serve the blocks also prompted objections, with one councillor saying it would be ‘chaotic’ and an ‘absolute shambles’ The Liberal Democrats ’ Meena Minnis said: “It’s a brownfield site and it does need sorting out because it looks awful, but I feel like it’s a bit big for the space. I would love some housing to be built there, we need housing anyway and I think this is a good place for it to be

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester EasyJet flight makes sharp U-turn after declaring emergency over North Sea EasyJet said the flight returned to Manchester Airport due to "a technical issue with the aircraft" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inno An EasyJet flight heading to Germany has made a sharp mid-air U-turn and returned to Manchester after declaring an emergency over the North Sea The flight, EZY32GY, from Manchester to Hamburg sparked concern on Wednesday evening (September 23) after declaring an emergency mid-air and turning back near Amsterdam According to Flight Radar, the aircraft took off at 7.15pm - one hour and 15 minutes after its scheduled departure time. The flight then squawked 7700 and turned around approximately 30 minutes after takeoff Squawk 7700 is the universal aviation transponder code used by pilots to signal a general in-flight emergency The real-time aviation alert service Squawk wrote on X shortly after 8pm: "An AIRBUS A-320 (EZY32GY) is squawking 7700 — declaring an emergency at 34,000 ft near Amsterdam, Netherlands."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Longstanding Oldham Labour councillor will not stand for re-election Coun Dr Zahid Chauhan OBE was first elected as a Labour councillor for the council ward of Alexandra in 2013. Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 18:52, 23 Se A longstanding Oldham councillor and former Mayor has announced he will not stand for re-election when voters go to the polls again in 2027 Coun Dr Zahid Chauhan OBE was first elected as a Labour councillor for the council ward of Alexandra in 2013. He is an NHS GP and the founder of the Homeless Friendly charity During his time as councillor, he served as Mayor for two years, was awarded Honorary Freedom of the Borough of Oldham , and recently campaigned on parking issues at the Royal Oldham Hospital. He has also previously served as the cabinet member overseeing health and social care In this role, Coun Chauhan said he was proud of making national history by launch a pop-up vaccination clinic for people experiencing homelessness. He also made sure two nurses Jean Purdy and Muriel Harris who had helped bring the first test-tube baby into the world were recognis After announcing he will be stepping down in May 2027, Coun Chauhan’s time as councillor will now end at the next set of local elections

Georgie Wright was found dead by her sister at her house on Sunday September 13 Emergency services were called to Dinsdale Drive where the 29-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene. The circumstances surrounding her death remain unknown and her case has been referred to a coroner's court According to her family, Georgie was in the process of 'turning her life around' after years of battling with mental health issues. Georgie was one of seven siblings and was known for her 'cheeky' personality and love of snakes "She was very cheeky, very funny, very quick-witted," said her sister Jessica. "She liked having a joke, she was fun to be around and always made me laugh "She was very caring as well; she would do her best to help you."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hollingworth Lake New Heywood mum, 27, rushed to hospital with life-threatening condition eight weeks after giving birth Matt Smith, from Heywood, is now taking on a major challenge to raise funds after the couple's terrifying ordeal News Elizabeth Co A Heywood man is taking on a gruelling 40-mile run to raise awareness of a rare form of thrombosis after his partner suffered a life-threatening blood clot following the birth of their daughter Matt Smith is running 40 miles around Hollingworth Lake on November 21, kicking off at 5am in support of Thrombosis UK , after his partner Charlotte, 27, developed a blood clot on the left side of her brain just weeks after giving birth by caesarean section Charlotte, from Heywood, developed a severe headache around eight to nine weeks after her C-section. The following night, she suffered two seizures and was rushed to hospital, where a CT scan revealed the clot, according to Matt Doctors diagnosed Charlotte with cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST), a rare form of thrombosis affecting the veins that drain blood from the brain Matt said Charlotte's pregnancy and C-section had increased her risk of developing the condition, despite her not having been identified as high-risk beforehand

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The following day, police swooped again, this time at a large stone brick property on Lancaster Road in Salford , understood to be a men’s hostel, and during a raid on a flat in Liverpool Eventually, police confirmed that counter terror officers had arrested two men under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000 And as our crime reporter John Scheerhout has revealed , the police investigation is thought to concern an alleged imminent threat to the Jewish community, which they believe has now been thwarted The investigation is set to be extended further, into Cheetham Hill and Heaton Park , the Manchester Evening News understands. And he believes its down to weight loss medications such as Mounjaro Writing on X he said: "You can tell Ozempic and Mounjaro are popular... in our Timpson shops we have seen a 680% increase in the number of free holes in customers belts we've been doing this year." Some estimates suggest around 2.4 million people in the UK are prescribed weight loss medications . The vast majority of people taking the drugs semaglutide (Wegovy for weight loss or Ozempic for diabetes) and Mounjaro pay privately owing to restrictions on who can access the med In June, the medicines regulator approved Wegovy in tablet form

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Hollingworth Lake New Heywood mum, 27, rushed to hospital with life-threatening condition eight weeks after giving birth Matt Smith, from Heywood, is now taking on a major challenge to raise funds after the couple's terrifying ordeal News Elizabeth Co A Heywood man is taking on a gruelling 40-mile run to raise awareness of a rare form of thrombosis after his partner suffered a life-threatening blood clot following the birth of their daughter Matt Smith is running 40 miles around Hollingworth Lake on November 21, kicking off at 5am in support of Thrombosis UK , after his partner Charlotte, 27, developed a blood clot on the left side of her brain just weeks after giving birth by caesarean section Charlotte, from Heywood, developed a severe headache around eight to nine weeks after her C-section. The following night, she suffered two seizures and was rushed to hospital, where a CT scan revealed the clot, according to Matt Doctors diagnosed Charlotte with cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST), a rare form of thrombosis affecting the veins that drain blood from the brain Matt said Charlotte's pregnancy and C-section had increased her risk of developing the condition, despite her not having been identified as high-risk beforehand

title: 'It's my entire career, and it's just been taken away. They saw an opportunity and they took it'

evidence_packet.title: 'It's my entire career, and it's just been taken away. They saw an opportunity and they took it'

They saw an opportunity and they took it' 'It's every artist's worst nightmare - but everyone has been so generous' Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 06:14, 24 Sep A Manchester makeup artist h
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre 'It's my entire career, and it's just been taken away. They saw an opportunity and they took it' 'It's every artist's worst nightmare - but everyone has been so generous' Comments News Greta Simpson Senior Reporter 06:14, 24 Sep A Manchester makeup artist has been blown away by support from the public after her kit, worth thousands of pounds, was stolen in Manchester city centre Talie Emslie, 29, had left her makeup kit and brush bag, which she estimates to be worth around £5,000, in her boyfriend's car in a car park near Piccadilly Station on Saturday night (September 19) "A brick had been put through the window, and everything had gone," Talie, who hails from Scotland, told the M.E.N. "It is every makeup artist's worst nightmare "I've been building this up for the past five years. I'm self-made, I don't have family I can fall back on or ask for financial help. This is a big deal to me "It's my entire career, it's been built up by me working to get to this point, and it's just been taken away. They saw an opportunity and they took it."

evidence_packet.lead: Greater Manchester Combined Authority The 'significant' threat of a major cyber attack on Greater Manchester - and what could happen Leaders around the region are set to meet for a cyber security discussion which will be partly in secret.

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Combined Authority The 'significant' threat of a major cyber attack on Greater Manchester - and what could happen Leaders around the region are set to meet for a cyber security discussion which will be partly in secret. View 3 Image Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 05:58, 24 Sep 2026 Updated 06:35, 24 Sep 2026 A successful cyber attack against Greater Manchester could put police GPS systems out of use and stop doctors accessing vital health data in an emergency, an expert has said in a fri While it may sound like the plot to a science fiction film, the risk of such an attack against the region is ‘significant and persistent’, said Ali Kashif Bashir, Professor of computer networks and cybersecurity at Manchester Metropolitan University The warning comes as a new report from the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) said the region is in a ‘hostile threat landscape’ and is facing major risks from cybercriminals and other countries Leaders across Greater Manchester are meeting on Monday (September 21) in a gathering which includes a deep-dive into cyber security. Part of the discussion will be held behind closed doors with no press or public access permitted According to GMCA papers, attackers are actively trying to disrupt Greater Manchester’s emergency services, spread disinformation, and interfere with democracy

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport EasyJet offered dad £150 after 11-hour Manchester Airport delay, what came next was a 'kick in the face' 'I wouldn't fly with easyJet again' Comments News Chris Slater Senior Reporter 05:57, 24 Sep 2026 View 3 Images Stephen Gilfoyl A dad who says his family lost out on a day of their £4,000 holiday after a diversion and delays of around 11 hours has hit out after he was initially offered just £150 compensation Stephen Gilfoyle, 39, was due to fly out from Manchester Airport to Antalya in Turkey with easyJet on August 31 for a week-long all-inclusive package holiday with his wife and eight-year-old daughter However, shortly before they were due to board a coach to take them to the plane for their 7:45am flight, they were told they would be delayed as the captain was 'ill.' After a delay of two hours, they did board the plane, but once they were seated, they were told they would be further delayed due to ' weather problems.' They eventually took off five hours late; however, Stephen said the disruption did not end there Just two hours into the four-hour flight, he says, they were told they would be diverting to Milan as members of the cabin crew would go over their allotted hours if they continued to their destination

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Trafford Council ‘Too big’ and an ‘absolute shambles', but 300 new homes have just been been approved Councillors agreed the site is an 'eyesore' and needs 'sorting out' but some did not think this was the right approach Comments News Hannah Richardso Councillors fear the project is ‘too big’ and parking plans are an ‘absolute shambles', but plans for 300 new homes have been approved for Old Trafford The plan flats on the site of a ‘derelict’ petrol station and disused multi-storey car park in Chester Road left Trafford council’s planning committee divided on Tuesday night (September 22). The scheme will see the existing structures demolished and two blocks of 286 apartments While all on the committee agreed that the ‘eyesore’ land needed to be redeveloped, not everyone was convinced that this scheme was the right solution. The debate saw a vote to reject the proposal defeated Concerns were raised by some members that the plan was ‘too big’ for the area and would ‘dwarf everything else’. The provision of just seven parking spaces to serve the blocks also prompted objections, with one councillor saying it would be ‘chaotic’ and an ‘absolute shambles’ The Liberal Democrats ’ Meena Minnis said: “It’s a brownfield site and it does need sorting out because it looks awful, but I feel like it’s a bit big for the space. evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Airport Manchester EasyJet flight makes sharp U-turn after declaring emergency over North Sea EasyJet said the flight returned to Manchester Airport due to "a technical issue with the aircraft" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inno An EasyJet flight heading to
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Airport Manchester EasyJet flight makes sharp U-turn after declaring emergency over North Sea EasyJet said the flight returned to Manchester Airport due to "a technical issue with the aircraft" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inno An EasyJet flight heading to
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Airport Manchester EasyJet flight makes sharp U-turn after declaring emergency over North Sea EasyJet said the flight returned to Manchester Airport due to "a technical issue with the aircraft" Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Inno An EasyJet flight heading to Germany has made a sharp mid-air U-turn and returned to Manchester after declaring an emergency over the North Sea The flight, EZY32GY, from Manchester to Hamburg sparked concern on Wednesday evening (September 23) after declaring an emergency mid-air and turning back near Amsterdam According to Flight Radar, the aircraft took off at 7.15pm - one hour and 15 minutes after its scheduled departure time. The flight then squawked 7700 and turned around approximately 30 minutes after takeoff Squawk 7700 is the universal aviation transponder code used by pilots to signal a general in-flight emergency The real-time aviation alert service Squawk wrote on X shortly after 8pm: "An AIRBUS A-320 (EZY32GY) is squawking 7700 — declaring an emergency at 34,000 ft near Amsterdam, Netherlands."

Then he got straight on his moped and did the very thing that landed him behind bars in the first place And the police were ready and waiting for him to do so. Between Southall Street and what is now the AO Arena the 59-year-old Sikh, known as Gyani Ji, was stopped and ticketed seven times His crime was refusing to remove his turban to wear a helmet while riding his 50cc Honda moped. And his small but persistent acts of civil disobedience would result in a landmark change in the law Gyani Ji was an activist who played a pivotal role in advancing Sikh religious rights in the UK. Born in Punjab, India, now Pakistan after partition, he moved to Manchester in 1948 and went on to help establish one of Europe's earliest Sikh temples in Moss Side His first high-profile campaign came in 1959 when he was denied a job as bus conductor due to uniform requirements which meant he would have to remove his turban and wear a cap. Georgie Wright was found dead by her sister at her house on Sunday September 13 Emergency services were called to Dinsdale Drive where the 29-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene. The circumstances surrounding her death remain unknown and her case has been referred to a coroner's court According to her family, Georgie was in the process of 'turning her life around' after years of battling with mental health issues. Georgie was one of seven siblings and was known for her 'cheeky' personality and love of snakes "She was very cheeky, very funny, very quick-witted," said her sister Jessica. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The following day, police swooped again, this time at a large stone brick property on Lancaster Road in Salford , understood to be a men’s hostel, and during a raid on a flat in Liverpool Eventually, police confirmed that counter terror officers had arrested two men under Section 41 of the Terrorism Act 2000 And as our crime reporter John Scheerhout has revealed , the police investigation is thought to concern an alleged imminent threat to the Jewish community, which they believe has now been thwarted The investigation is set to be extended further, into Cheetham Hill and Heaton Park , the Manchester Evening News understands. And the Metropolitan Police, leading the investigation, stressed 'there is no information to suggest any wider threat to the public' View 6 Images The cordon on Newton Street (Image: Josh Pennington/Manchester Evening News) But as John says, there is clearly much more to this story than has yet been made public

And he believes its down to weight loss medications such as Mounjaro Writing on X he said: "You can tell Ozempic and Mounjaro are popular... in our Timpson shops we have seen a 680% increase in the number of free holes in customers belts we've been doing this year." Some estimates suggest around 2.4 million people in the UK are prescribed weight loss medications . The vast majority of people taking the drugs semaglutide (Wegovy for weight loss or Ozempic for diabetes) and Mounjaro pay privately owing to restrictions on who can access the med In June, the medicines regulator approved Wegovy in tablet form

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester City Centre The long fightback against 'vile' nightlife videos A former Rochdale councillor is sparking a debate View 6 Images 'Manchester nightlife' videos have flooded social media in recent years - could a fightback be underway? (Image: News Stephen Topping Senior reporter 06:06, 23 Sep 2026 Updated 07:26, 23 Sep 2026 They have flooded social media and left women facing a barrage of abuse from strangers. Yet when police tried to prosecute those responsible, nothing could be done under criminal law But could that situation change? A Liberal Democrat MP and former Rochdale councillor has opened up a significant debate on the filming and sharing of videos without consent - including the creepy ‘Manchester nightlife’ footage which is littered across the web Wera Hobhouse introduced a presentation bill on the issue to Parliament earlier this year, which fell before the summer recess. She also raised the subject during Andy Burnham ’s first day in the House of Commons as Prime Minister earlier this month Now, Ms Hobhouse has secured the backing of her party in calling for the law to be tightened so 'sexualised covert filming' and its sharing online is a criminal offence. She could also introduce a new private member’s bill to Parliament, to spark a wider debate among MPs “I think it needs a change in legislation,” Ms Hobhouse told the Manchester Evening News . “I don’t think you can ask these guys to just ‘be nice’.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Firefighters in Greater Manchester will honour a retained firefighter who drowned trying to save a missing teenager, in a case that changed water rescue practice across the UK Sub Officer Paul Metcalf, based at Ramsbottom Fire Station, entered a lake at Holcombe Brook near Bury on 5 September 1999 after a 16-year-old boy failed to resurface. Young people had been jumping into the water using a rope swing Mr Metcalf and his crew went into the water with general purpose lines attached to their waists for recovery which was standard practice at the time The lake was up to 40 feet deep and his line snagged on underwater debris As colleagues and police pulled the line to bring him ashore, unaware it was caught, he was pulled under water taking around 15 minutes to recover him He tragically died in hospital shortly afterwards

A world first falls prevention pilot in Greater Manchester has shown that identifying older people at risk of falling and offering them early support can help improve their participation in strength and balance classes, confidence and independence.. . The eFalls pilot, launched in Wigan in February 2025, used routine NHS data to identify more than 1,100 people aged 65 and over who were at increased risk of falling in the following year.. . People identified through the pilot were contacted through their GP practice and invited for a health check, with support offered to help reduce their risk of falling.. . Almost eight in 10 people offered support chose to take part, with many going on to attend local strength and balance classes through the Falls Management Exercise (FaME) programme.. . The evaluation found that the benefits of taking part went beyond helping people improve their balance.. . Participants reported feeling stronger when getting up from a chair and walking outside, as well as having greater confidence to go out alone and less worry about falling.. . Some people also reported sleeping better, feeling brighter and enjoying being active again. The pilot also found that the way people were approached was important in encouraging them to take up the offer of support.. . evidence_packet.evidence_text: In 2028 it will be 100 years since women were granted the right to vote on equal terms with men Although some women were granted the right to vote in 1918, it was not until 1928 that all women over the age of 21 were granted the vote regardless of their occupation, wealth or ownership of property To mark this hugely significant milestone a Council motion has been set out to recognise and celebrate this moment in history It is no secret that Manchester played a huge part in the Women’s Suffrage movement. The Pankhurst name is known across the globe and is a byword for resilience and a refusal to give in to apparent insurmountable odds In 2018 a statue of Emmeline Pankhurst was proudly installed in St Peter’s Square and has since become a rallying point for people across the city to have their voices heard, and acts as a powerful reminder that history was made by women who refused to give up But the Pankhursts were also joined by thousands of ordinary Mancunian women whose names have been lost to history, but whose legacy still lives on a century later

title: Bolton company boss who sold £500k of illegal medical devices sentenced

evidence_packet.title: Bolton company boss who sold £500k of illegal medical devices sentenced
evidence_packet.lead: Kenneth Harrison co-founded Medicina Ltd, a legitimate company selling medical goods, in 1991 but over the years began to regard proper testing and certification as merely "red tape" and an inconvenience, a court heard Manchester Crown Court was told he had also encouraged his st
evidence_packet.summary: Kenneth Harrison co-founded Medicina Ltd, a legitimate company selling medical goods, in 1991 but over the years began to regard proper testing and certification as merely "red tape" and an inconvenience, a court heard Manchester Crown Court was told he had also encouraged his st
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Kenneth Harrison co-founded Medicina Ltd, a legitimate company selling medical goods, in 1991 but over the years began to regard proper testing and certification as merely "red tape" and an inconvenience, a court heard Manchester Crown Court was told he had also encouraged his staff to cover up his dishonesty by selling goods with false safety approval markings The 70-year-old, from Bolton, Greater Manchester, was convicted of five fraud offences between 2010 and 2014, following a 10-week trial earlier this year The hearing was told Harrison had sold goods bearing false "CE" markings to hospitals and clinics in the UK and worldwide, misleading buyers into believing they had passed EU-wide safety and regulatory approval Judge Timothy Smith sentenced Harrison to 175 hours of unpaid work alongside the suspended jail sentence He also disqualified the him from being a company director for eight years

evidence_packet.lead: Neil Cox wore nothing but a small bag over his shoulder, in which he carried a copy of the naturism guidance from the College of Policing and his mobile phone Two women had been left "confused and scared" after seeing the naked walker, a court heard Cox was convicted of disorderl
evidence_packet.summary: Neil Cox wore nothing but a small bag over his shoulder, in which he carried a copy of the naturism guidance from the College of Policing and his mobile phone Two women had been left "confused and scared" after seeing the naked walker, a court heard Cox was convicted of disorderl
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Neil Cox wore nothing but a small bag over his shoulder, in which he carried a copy of the naturism guidance from the College of Policing and his mobile phone Two women had been left "confused and scared" after seeing the naked walker, a court heard Cox was convicted of disorderly or threatening behaviour and fined £800 following the incident near Macclesfield, Cheshire, on 22 August 2023. His second appeal has now been rejected A previous appeal against his conviction was first dismissed at Chester Crown Court in November 2024 During the latest hearing, Dame Victoria Sharp, sitting with Mrs Justice Hill at the High Court in Manchester, said Cox had been waiting for a shop to open at about 06.30 BST when he walked past Det Ch Insp Mark Whittaker and later two women The detective, who was out for a morning run, carried on past Cox after "making his disapproval known" but then turned around to arrest him

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.summary: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live […] The post Beat the Jams Autumn season announced appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Finish work and unwind with live music from Manchester’s best jazz musicians. Beat the Jams live series showcases the very best of the jazz scene, at short rush hour gigs from 6pm at Band on the Wall. What better way to avoid those endless queues, chaotic traffic and stressful homeward journeys? Clock off and skip the rush-hour traffic while you watch live jazz and make the most of our happy hour deals from 5–7pm: £4.50 pints / 2 for £15 cocktails / £15 bottles of wine + pizzas from £5! The new season kicks off on 24 September with tenor saxophonist Dean Masser and pianist Richard Wetherall, followed by: 7 October – Anna Chandler-King Quartet Leeds based saxophonist and composer Anna joins us again for Beat the Jams, this time with her own band. Anna’s thoughtful and inventive compositions are firm favourites of us at Beat the Jams and her quartet promises to be a unique rush hour busting treat! 16 November – Sam Lightwing Quartet Saxophonist and composer Sam Lightwing brings presents brand new music for his thrilling young quartet, showcasing Sam’s original compositions, which blend classic mainstream jazz grooves with modern flavours of post-pop and latin, all wrapped up in the language of contemporary sax giants such as Chris Potter, Seamus Blake and Joshua Redman. 15 December – Svarc/Devine/Walsh with Richard Iles The band combines deep pocket, fearless interplay and a shared love of exploration. Expect everything from soulful melodies and infectious rhythms to moments of exhilarating collective improvisation, delivered with the chemistry that only world-class musicians can create. Tickets from £13 per show, or £42 for a season ticket

title: Young Musician's Summer School

evidence_packet.title: Young Musician's Summer School
evidence_packet.lead: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer!
evidence_packet.summary: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! […] The post Young Musician’s Summer School appeared first on Band on the Wall
evidence_packet.evidence_text: We’re inviting young people to explore music for film and compose their own soundtrack this summer! Whether your child already attends our Saturday Music Club, or just wants to try something new, our Young Musician’s Summer School is suitable for all abilities! Across this 5 day course, we’ll be exploring music for film, and working on composing music for the silent film ‘A Trip to the Moon’. The course will conclude with a live performance soundtracking the film for family and friends. We welcome all abilities and instruments to take part in this course. You can bring your own instruments, but we have keyboards, guitars, bass, violins, drums and percussion on site which can be used if you don’t have an instrument. The next phase of AI is likely to be much less about what a model can demonstrate on a screen and much more about whether businesses can deploy it securel There is also an opportunity for Manchester and the wider North that goes beyond simply increasing AI adoption. The region already has strengths across advanced materials, computing infrastructure, cyber security, health innovation and emerging technologies such as quantum. The c The previous day also saw an Innovation Day, where 20 of the region’s most innovative startups pitched to the biggest organisations working across defence, national security and technology, then took part in a number of Round Table discussions Here’s our write up of the full day’s conference

evidence_packet.evidence_text: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No From the potential impact of greater devolved powers in Manchester to the role of No.10 North, Katie explores how national and regional government can work more effectively with the tech sector - and why the North’s different tech ecosystems need to be better connected rather tha Greater devolution will be positive for Manchester’s tech ecosystem. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. It should mean earlier engagement

evidence_packet.evidence_text: The best industry experiences don’t just show young people what a career in tech could look like - they give them the opportunity to become part of it That’s exactly what Hippo helped create through their support of Manchester Digital’s T Connect programme, providing students with exposure to the industry, practical experience and the confidence to take their next steps into tech Hippo’s involvement began with a problem-solving session for T Connect students, where their team ran activities designed to encourage creative thinking, collaboration and approaching challenges in the way technology teams do every day Following this session, Hippo selected two learners - Ahmed Abdul Karim and Edu Samuel Manuel - to take part in a 36-day industry placement with the business The placement gave Ahmed and Edu the opportunity to work alongside Hippo’s teams from their Leeds office, contributing to projects for the Department for Education and gaining first-hand experience of working in a professional technology environment Throughout their placements, they were treated as members of the team, gaining insight into the full process of delivering digital products - from technical development and problem solving through to collaboration and communication

The garden is the result of an ambitious programme of fundraising, design and craftsmanship, creating a striking new attraction within RHS Bridgewater’s seven-acre Chinese Streamside G Developed in partnership with Yangzhou City, the China Flower Association, Greater Manchester’s Chinese community and the RHS , it combines authentic Chinese architecture, horticulture and cultural traditions in a landscape inspired by the historic scholars’ gardens of Yangzhou The Yangzhou Scholars’ Garden has been meticulously crafted by skilled Chinese artisans and centres around four interconnected pavilions celebrating the scholarly arts of chess, music, calligraphy and painting. Every pathway, bridge and view has been designed to reveal beauty and Marcus Chilton-Jones, Head of RHS Bridgewater, said: “The opening of the Yangzhou Scholars’ Garden is a landmark moment for RHS Garden Bridgewater and for Greater Manchester “This remarkable international collaboration has created not only a beautiful garden, but a lasting symbol of friendship, cultural exchange and shared learning. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. evidence_packet.evidence_text: GM Business Growth Hub, are pleased to be hosting this event in partnership with Stockport Council Join us for a focused morning designed to help businesses explore and unlock international growth opportunities. This event will provide a practical overview of the global trade landscape , including key trends across priority sectors and markets, and what they mean for businesse Hear from experienced exporters who will share real-life examples, lessons learned and strategies for success in international markets You’ll also gain a clearer understanding of the support available for Greater Manchester businesses looking to grow internationally, and how to tap into this support For companies new to exporting or looking to build on existing international experience, you will leave this morning session with insights, connections, and an understanding of where to access the right support to take your next step Stay on after the formal sessions to network with peers and our speakers over lunch
